'''''Peperomia obtusifolia''''', also known as the '''baby rubberplant''', '''American rubber plant''', or  '''pepper face''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[genus]] ''[[Peperomia]]'' under the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Piperaceae]], native to Tropical America.<ref>{{cite web|title=Missouri Botanical Garden - ''Peperomia obtusifolia''|url=http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/gardens-gardening/your-garden/plant-finder/plant-details/kc/b609/peperomia-obtusifolia.aspx|accessdate=2013-05-25}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Peperomia obtusifolia |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/peperomia-obtusifolia/ |website=NC State University |access-date=10 May 2022}}</ref> The [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''obtusifolia'' means "blunt-leaved".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=9781845337315|pages=224}}</ref> The plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF/><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 75 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 22 April 2018}}</ref>

==Description==
The baby rubberplant is an [[evergreen]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] growing to {{convert|25|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall and broad with cupped leathery leaves and narrow spikes of white flowers up to {{convert|12|cm|0|abbr=on}} long, which grow in a shiny, winding manner and constitute the main decorative value of the plant.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

''P. obtusifolia'' is often confused with ''[[Peperomia magnoliifolia]]'', and some earlier botanists considered these two names merely synonyms for the same species. As dried specimens, the plants can look highly similar, though the difference can be seen more easily with living plants: ''P. obtusifolia'' leaves are waxy, while ''P. mangoliifolia'' leaves are considered fleshy. Due to the confusion, plants in collections or on sale may be falsely labelled.<ref>{{cite web |title=Peperomia obtusifolia |url=http://portal.cybertaxonomy.org/flora-guianas/cdm_dataportal/taxon/694bf1b9-c190-451c-9641-b714e0f98322 |website=Flora of the Guianas |access-date=5 August 2021}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
With a minimum temperature of {{convert|15|C|F|abbr=on}}, the baby rubberplant must be grown indoors in most [[temperateness|temperate]] regions. Although it needs high humidity, it does not require much care. Good lighting is enough to maintain the bright and intense colour of the leaves, though direct light causes discoloration. The stem is fleshy, so the plant does not need abundant or frequent watering. A popular [[houseplant]], numerous [[cultivars]] have been developed, some of which show leaf [[variegation]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Peperomia obtusifolia''|url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/106212/peperomia-obtusifolia/details | access-date = 11 February 2023}}</ref>

==Pests and diseases==
In general, the baby rubberplant is a resistant plant, though it can have problems with [[aphids]] and [[mealybug]]s. As with many houseplants, excessive watering can cause [[root rot]].<ref>Dawid Longman: Nurturing house plants . Warsaw: PWR and L, 1997. {{ISBN|83-09-01559-3}}</ref>
